about: The four default color sets for figma-webdesigner and figma-appdesigner. Every value was read from the page named in `source` on the `checked` date. This file is the same in both tools; change it in both.

roles.surface: cards, panels, sheets: one step off the ground
roles.border: hairlines and dividers (decorative: not relied on to find a control)
roles.accent: the one color for the main action and for emphasis
roles.on-accent: text and icons that sit on the accent

wireframe.name: Wireframe
wireframe.about: Greys only, for drawing a layout before any color goes on. It is not a brand set and nobody ships it. In Figma it is one more mode of the Palette variables, so a wireframe becomes a styled screen by switching the frame's mode, not by redrawing.

palettes.name: Bear Brown
palettes.how_read: CSS custom properties of the live page (.light and .dark)
notes: Terracotta #D97757 is decoration only: it is under 3:1 on the cream ground, so never use it for text or for a control's only boundary.
Muted ink #9E8C6C is for large text only.
The role names here (ground, ink, ...) are this tool's. The site calls them --p-bg, --p-ink, --p-ink-soft, --m-accent and so on.

palettes.name: Brutalist
palettes.how_read: computed colors of the rendered home page, plus its .dark custom properties
notes: This is what brutalist.art shows: black on white with slate greys and solid black buttons. The eight browns are declared in the site's stylesheet but no element on the home page uses them.
The Brutalist film toolkit uses a different set (cream #FAF9F5, warm ink #3D3929, one terracotta #D97757). That set is the Bear Brown palette here.

Dark: the site's solid buttons stayed black when the page was switched to dark, which is nearly invisible on #020817. The dark accent here is the site's light foreground instead. That is this tool's choice, not the site's.
Slate secondary text #64748B on the slate surface #F1F5F9 is 4.34:1, just under 4.5:1. Put small secondary text on the white ground, or use the ink on cards.

palettes.name: Northeastern
palettes.how_read: the Brand Center color page (published hex values)
notes: The Brand Center publishes no dark mode, so this palette has a light mode only.
Red goes in every piece, but not as a sea of red. Gold is reserved (about 5% of a design at most, mostly the Office of the President).
Units may not have their own identity palettes. Colors do not give permission to use Northeastern's logos or name: those have their own rules.
The Brand Center's type is FF Real Head Pro (licensed). Lato is the free stand-in used here.

palettes.name: Humanitarians AI
palettes.how_read: CSS custom properties of the live page (:root and .dark)
notes: Secondary text here is dim gray #4A4D4F. The site's own muted text (mist, about #7D7D7D) is under 4.5:1 on white, so keep mist for large text.
Warm clay #A89068 is a fill and a decoration: dark text on it passes, white text on it does not.
Dark: the red #B20000 against the dark ground is 2.47:1, under the 3:1 a control's edge needs. A dark-mode red button must carry a clear label (white on it passes) or a lighter outline.
